51	def _validate_rules(rules: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
52	    if not isinstance(rules, list):
53	        raise ValueError("rules must be a list of rule dicts")
54	    seen: set[tuple[str, str, int]] = set()
55	    for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
56	        field = f"rules[{index}]"
57	        if not isinstance(rule, dict) or set(rule) != _RULE_KEYS:
58	            raise ValueError(
59	                f"{field} must be a dict with exactly the keys "
60	                "id, ver, source, priority, from, to, when, result"
61	            )
62	        _check_non_empty_str(rule["id"], f"{field}.id")
63	        _check_non_empty_str(rule["result"], f"{field}.result")
64	        ver = _check_int(rule["ver"], f"{field}.ver")
65	        if ver < 1:
66	            raise ValueError(f"{field}.ver must be a positive integer")
67	        source = rule["source"]
68	        if source not in _SOURCES:
69	            raise ValueError(f"{field}.source must be 'law' or 'org'")
70	        _check_int(rule["priority"], f"{field}.priority")
71	        frm = _check_time(rule["from"], f"{field}.from")
72	        to = rule["to"]
73	        if to is not None:
74	            _check_time(to, f"{field}.to")
75	            if not frm < to:
76	                raise ValueError(f"{field} requires from < to")
77	        when = rule["when"]
78	        if when is not None:
79	            _check_fact_map(when, f"{field}.when")
80	        key = (source, rule["id"], ver)
81	        if key in seen:
82	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate (source, id, ver): {key!r}")
83	        seen.add(key)
84	    return rules

87	def _compare(a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
88	    if a["source"] != b["source"]:
89	        return -1 if a["source"] == "law" else 1
90	    if a["priority"] != b["priority"]:
91	        return -1 if a["priority"] > b["priority"] else 1
92	    if a["from"] != b["from"]:
93	        return -1 if a["from"] > b["from"] else 1
94	    if a["id"] != b["id"]:
95	        return -1 if a["id"] < b["id"] else 1
96	    if a["ver"] != b["ver"]:
97	        return -1 if a["ver"] > b["ver"] else 1
98	    return 0

101	def _effective_rules(at: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
102	    """Validate, select effective-at-``at`` rules, keep the highest ver per
103	    ``(source, id)``, and rank them exactly as :func:`evaluate` does."""
104	    _check_time(at, "at")
105	    rules = _validate_rules(rules)
106	
107	    effective = [
108	        rule
109	        for rule in rules
110	        if rule["from"] <= at and (rule["to"] is None or at < rule["to"])
111	    ]
112	
113	    latest: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
114	    for rule in effective:
115	        key = (rule["source"], rule["id"])
116	        if key not in latest or rule["ver"] > latest[key]["ver"]:
117	            latest[key] = rule
118	
119	    ranked = list(latest.values())
120	    ranked.sort(key=cmp_to_key(_compare))
121	    return ranked

124	def _matches(rule: dict[str, Any], facts: dict[str, bool]) -> bool:
125	    """Return whether ``rule``'s ``when`` condition holds under ``facts``."""
126	    when = rule["when"]
127	    return when is None or all(
128	        key in facts and facts[key] == value for key, value in when.items()
129	    )

132	def _matched_rules(
133	    at: str, facts: dict[str, bool], rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
134	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
135	    """Return the matching rules in ranking order after validation.
136	
137	    Validation, latest-version selection, and ordering are exactly those of
138	    :func:`evaluate`.
139	    """
140	    _check_fact_map(facts, "facts")
141	    ranked = _effective_rules(at, rules)
142	    return [rule for rule in ranked if _matches(rule, facts)]

145	def evaluate(
146	    at: str, facts: dict[str, bool], rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
147	) -> tuple[str | None, list[str]]:
148	    """Evaluate versioned rules against facts at a UTC second timestamp.
149	
150	    Returns ``(decision, trace)`` where ``trace`` lists every matching rule as
151	    ``id@ver`` in ranking order and ``decision`` is the top rule's ``result``
152	    (``None`` with an empty trace when nothing matches).
153	    """
154	    matched = _matched_rules(at, facts, rules)
155	    if not matched:
156	        return None, []
157	    trace = [f"{rule['id']}@{rule['ver']}" for rule in matched]
158	    return matched[0]["result"], trace

161	def _conditions_compatible(a: dict[str, bool] | None, b: dict[str, bool] | None) -> bool:
162	    """Return whether two ``when`` conditions can hold simultaneously.
163	
164	    ``None`` means unconstrained. Conditions are incompatible only when they
165	    assign opposite booleans to a shared key.
166	    """
167	    if a is None or b is None:
168	        return True
169	    for key, value in a.items():
170	        if key in b and b[key] is not value:
171	            return False
172	    return True

175	def _snapshot_rule(rule: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
176	    """Return a deep-copied rule snapshot with stable key order.
177	
178	    Keys are ordered ``id, ver, source, priority, from, to, when, result``
179	    and ``when`` keys are sorted in Unicode code point order.
180	    """
181	    when = rule["when"]
182	    if when is not None:
183	        when = {key: when[key] for key in sorted(when)}
184	    return {
185	        "id": rule["id"],
186	        "ver": rule["ver"],
187	        "source": rule["source"],
188	        "priority": rule["priority"],
189	        "from": rule["from"],
190	        "to": rule["to"],
191	        "when": when,
192	        "result": rule["result"],
193	    }

196	def _find_conflicts(ranked: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
197	    """List conflicts between ranked rules as ``winner``/``loser`` triples.
198	
199	    For ranked indices ``i < j``, a pair conflicts when the results differ
200	    and the ``when`` conditions can hold simultaneously; the earlier rule is
201	    the winner.
202	    """
203	    conflicts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
204	    for i in range(len(ranked)):
205	        winner = ranked[i]
206	        for j in range(i + 1, len(ranked)):
207	            loser = ranked[j]
208	            if winner["result"] != loser["result"] and _conditions_compatible(
209	                winner["when"], loser["when"]
210	            ):
211	                conflicts.append(
212	                    {
213	                        "winner": [winner["source"], winner["id"], winner["ver"]],
214	                        "loser": [loser["source"], loser["id"], loser["ver"]],
215	                    }
216	                )
217	    return conflicts
218

220	def compile_rules(at: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
221	    """Compile the rules effective at ``at`` into rules and conflicts.
222	
223	    Reuses the full validation of :func:`evaluate` for ``at`` and ``rules``
224	    (raising ``ValueError`` on anything invalid), keeps rules in their
225	    ``[from, to)`` window, retains only the highest ``ver`` per
226	    ``(source, id)``, and orders the survivors with :func:`evaluate`'s ranking.
227	
228	    ``conflicts`` lists, for ranked indices ``i < j``, pairs whose results
229	    differ and whose ``when`` conditions can hold simultaneously; the earlier
230	    rule is the winner. The returned structure is a deep copy with stable key
231	    order.
232	    """
233	    ranked = _effective_rules(at, rules)
234	    compiled_rules = [_snapshot_rule(rule) for rule in ranked]
235	    conflicts = _find_conflicts(ranked)
236	    return {"at": at, "rules": compiled_rules, "conflicts": conflicts}

239	def policy_attestation(at: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
240	    """Attest a :func:`compile_rules` result with a SHA-256 digest.
241	
242	    ``at`` and ``rules`` are validated exactly as in :func:`compile_rules`;
243	    any type, time, rule-field, ``[from, to)`` interval, or duplicate
244	    ``(source, id, ver)`` error raises ``ValueError`` without mutating the
245	    inputs.
246	
247	    Let ``policy`` be the :func:`compile_rules` result and let ``C`` be the
248	    UTF-8 bytes of ``json.dumps(policy, ensure_ascii=False,
249	    separators=(',', ':'))`` (with no trailing newline). Returns a deep copy
250	    with keys ``at``, ``policy``, ``digest``; ``policy`` keeps every
251	    :func:`compile_rules` key order, ordering, ``when`` Unicode code point
252	    sort, and ``conflicts`` order, and ``digest`` is the lowercase 64-char
253	    hex SHA-256 of ``C``. Equal-valued inputs yield byte-identical results.
254	    """
255	    policy = compile_rules(at, rules)
256	    canonical = json.dumps(policy, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
257	    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
258	    return {"at": at, "policy": copy.deepcopy(policy), "digest": digest}

264	def _conflict_identity(conflict: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str, int, str, str, int]:
265	    """Return the six-element identity of a conflict: winner then loser."""
266	    return tuple(conflict["winner"]) + tuple(conflict["loser"])

269	def policy_delta(
270	    from_at: str, to_at: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
271	) -> dict[str, Any]:
272	    """Diff the :func:`compile_rules` results at two UTC timestamps.

274	    Both timestamps must be valid UTC seconds of the form
275	    ``YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`` with ``from_at <= to_at``; ``rules`` is
276	    validated exactly as in :func:`compile_rules`. Any type, time,
277	    rule-structure, or ordering violation raises ``ValueError`` without
278	    mutating the inputs.
279	
280	    The rules effective at each timestamp are compiled separately and
281	    identified by ``(source, id)``. Returns a deep copy with keys ``from``,
282	    ``to``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``. ``rules`` lists, ordered by ``source``
283	    (``law`` before ``org``) then ``id`` in Unicode code point order, one
284	    entry per rule that was ``added`` (only at ``to_at``), ``removed`` (only
285	    at ``from_at``), or ``updated`` (present at both but with a different
286	    compiled value); identical rules are omitted. Each entry has keys
287	    ``source``, ``id``, ``kind``, ``before``, ``after``; ``before``/``after``
288	    are the corresponding compiled rule snapshots (with :func:`compile_rules`
289	    key order and ``when`` sorting) or ``None``.
290	
291	    ``conflicts`` has keys ``added``, ``removed``. A conflict's identity is
292	    the six-element value of its ``winner`` array followed by its ``loser``
293	    array. ``added`` lists, in the ``to_at`` compile order, the conflicts
294	    present only at ``to_at``; ``removed`` lists, in the ``from_at`` compile
295	    order, those present only at ``from_at``. Each conflict keeps the keys
296	    ``winner``, ``loser`` with deep-copied values. When nothing differs,
297	    ``rules`` is empty and both conflict arrays are empty.
298	    """
299	    _check_time(from_at, "from_at")
300	    _check_time(to_at, "to_at")
301	    if from_at > to_at:
302	        raise ValueError(f"from_at must not be after to_at: {from_at!r} > {to_at!r}")
303	    before_compiled = compile_rules(from_at, rules)
304	    after_compiled = compile_rules(to_at, rules)
305	
306	    before_rules = {
307	        (rule["source"], rule["id"]): rule for rule in before_compiled["rules"]
308	    }
309	    after_rules = {
310	        (rule["source"], rule["id"]): rule for rule in after_compiled["rules"]
311	    }
312	    entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
313	    for key in sorted(
314	        set(before_rules) | set(after_rules),
315	        key=lambda item: (_SOURCE_ORDER[item[0]], item[1]),
316	    ):
317	        before = before_rules.get(key)
318	        after = after_rules.get(key)
319	        if before is not None and after is not None and before == after:
320	            continue
321	        if before is None:
322	            kind = "added"
323	        elif after is None:
324	            kind = "removed"
325	        else:
326	            kind = "updated"
327	        entries.append(
328	            {
329	                "source": key[0],
330	                "id": key[1],
331	                "kind": kind,
332	                "before": before,
333	                "after": after,
334	            }
335	        )

338	    after_conflicts = after_compiled["conflicts"]
339	    before_identities = {_conflict_identity(c) for c in before_conflicts}
340	    after_identities = {_conflict_identity(c) for c in after_conflicts}
341	    added_conflicts = [

359	def policy_schedule(
360	    start: str, end: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
361	) -> dict[str, Any]:
362	    """Compile the policy at the rule boundaries inside a time range.
363	
364	    ``start`` and ``end`` must be valid UTC seconds of the form
365	    ``YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`` with ``start <= end``; ``rules`` is validated
366	    exactly as in :func:`compile_rules`. Any type, time, rule-structure, or
367	    ordering violation raises ``ValueError`` without mutating the inputs.
368	
369	    The candidate timestamps are ``start`` plus every rule ``from`` and
370	    non-``None`` ``to`` falling in ``(start, end]``, deduplicated and sorted
371	    ascending; :func:`compile_rules` is called at each candidate. The first
372	    point is always kept; for each later candidate the function computes
373	    :func:`policy_delta` from the previously kept point to the candidate and
374	    keeps the point unless that delta reports no changes at all (``rules``
375	    empty and both ``conflicts`` arrays empty).
376	
377	    Returns a deep copy with keys ``start``, ``end``, ``points``. Each point
378	    has keys ``at``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``, ``delta``; ``rules`` and
379	    ``conflicts`` are exactly the same-named :func:`compile_rules` values at
380	    ``at`` and keep that contract at every level. The first point's ``delta``
381	    is ``None``; a later point's ``delta`` is the full :func:`policy_delta`
382	    result described above.
383	    """
384	    _check_time(start, "start")
385	    _check_time(end, "end")
386	    if start > end:
387	        raise ValueError(f"start must not be after end: {start!r} > {end!r}")
388	    _validate_rules(rules)
389	    first = compile_rules(start, rules)
390	    candidates = {start}
391	    for rule in rules:
392	        for boundary in (rule["from"], rule["to"]):
393	            if boundary is not None and start < boundary <= end:
394	                candidates.add(boundary)
395	    points = [
396	        {
397	            "at": first["at"],
398	            "rules": first["rules"],
399	            "conflicts": first["conflicts"],
400	            "delta": None,
401	        }
402	    ]
403	    previous_at = start
404	    for at in sorted(candidates - {start}):
405	        compiled = compile_rules(at, rules)
406	        delta = policy_delta(previous_at, at, rules)
407	        if (
408	            not delta["rules"]
409	            and not delta["conflicts"]["added"]
410	            and not delta["conflicts"]["removed"]
411	        ):

413	        points.append(
414	            {
415	                "at": compiled["at"],
416	                "rules": compiled["rules"],

425	def policy_schedule_attestation(
426	    start: str, end: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
427	) -> dict[str, Any]:
428	    """Attest a :func:`policy_schedule` result with a SHA-256 hash chain.
429	
430	    ``start``, ``end``, and ``rules`` are validated exactly as in
431	    :func:`policy_schedule`; any invalid value raises ``ValueError`` without
432	    mutating the inputs.
433	
434	    Let ``S`` be the :func:`policy_schedule` result. Returns a deep copy with
435	    top-level keys ``start``, ``end``, ``root``, ``points``; ``start`` and
436	    ``end`` come from ``S`` and ``points`` keeps ``S``'s point order. Each
437	    point has keys ``at``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``, ``delta``, ``previous``,
438	    ``digest``; the first four equal the corresponding ``S`` point at every
439	    level and keep its key order. The first point's ``previous`` is 64 ASCII
440	    ``0`` characters; every later point's ``previous`` is the previous
441	    point's ``digest``.
442	
443	    Let ``C`` be the UTF-8 bytes (with no newline) of
444	    ``json.dumps`` applied to the current point restricted to the keys
445	    ``at``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``, ``delta`` in that order, with
446	    ``ensure_ascii=False`` and ``separators=(',', ':')``. ``digest`` is the
447	    lowercase 64-char hex SHA-256 of the ASCII bytes of ``previous`` followed
448	    immediately by ``C``; ``root`` is the last point's ``digest``.
449	    Equal-valued inputs yield byte-identical results.
450	    """
451	    schedule = policy_schedule(start, end, rules)
452	    points: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
453	    previous = "0" * 64
454	    digest = previous
455	    for point in schedule["points"]:
456	        content = {
457	            "at": point["at"],
458	            "rules": copy.deepcopy(point["rules"]),
459	            "conflicts": copy.deepcopy(point["conflicts"]),
460	            "delta": copy.deepcopy(point["delta"]),
461	        }
462	        canonical = json.dumps(content, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
463	        digest = hashlib.sha256(
464	            previous.encode("ascii") + canonical.encode("utf-8")
465	        ).hexdigest()
466	        attested = dict(content)
467	        attested["previous"] = previous
468	        attested["digest"] = digest
469	        points.append(attested)
470	        previous = digest
471	    return {
472	        "start": schedule["start"],
473	        "end": schedule["end"],
474	        "root": digest,
475	        "points": points,
476	    }
477

677	def _check_schedule_point_semantics(
678	    point: dict[str, Any],
679	    index: int,
680	    previous: dict[str, Any] | None,
681	) -> None:
682	    """Check one normalized point against the schedule semantics.
683	
684	    The point's ``rules`` must be effective at its ``at``, unique per
685	    ``(source, id)``, and ranked exactly as :func:`compile_rules` ranks them;
686	    ``conflicts`` must equal the conflicts derived from those rules. A later
687	    point's ``delta`` must span from the previous point's ``at`` to this
688	    point's ``at`` and exactly match the :func:`policy_delta` of the two
689	    adjacent snapshots, and must not be empty.
690	    """
691	    field = f"points[{index}]"
692	    at = point["at"]
693	    rules = point["rules"]
694	    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
695	    for rule_index, rule in enumerate(rules):
696	        if not (rule["from"] <= at and (rule["to"] is None or at < rule["to"])):
697	            raise ValueError(
698	                f"{field}.rules[{rule_index}] is not effective at {field}.at"
699	            )
700	        key = (rule["source"], rule["id"])
701	        if key in seen:
702	            raise ValueError(f"{field}.rules has duplicate (source, id): {key!r}")
703	        seen.add(key)
704	    for rule_index in range(len(rules) - 1):
705	        if _compare(rules[rule_index], rules[rule_index + 1]) > 0:
706	            raise ValueError(
707	                f"{field}.rules are not in compile_rules ranking order"
708	            )
709	    if point["conflicts"] != _find_conflicts(rules):
710	        raise ValueError(
711	            f"{field}.conflicts do not equal the conflicts derived from "
712	            f"{field}.rules"
713	        )
714	    if index == 0:
715	        return
716	    assert previous is not None
717	    delta = point["delta"]
718	    if delta["from"] != previous["at"] or delta["to"] != at:
719	        raise ValueError(
720	            f"{field}.delta from/to must equal the previous point's at and "
721	            f"{field}.at"
722	        )
723	    before_rules = {
724	        (rule["source"], rule["id"]): rule for rule in previous["rules"]
725	    }
726	    after_rules = {(rule["source"], rule["id"]): rule for rule in rules}
727	    expected_entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
728	    for key in sorted(
729	        set(before_rules) | set(after_rules),
730	        key=lambda item: (_SOURCE_ORDER[item[0]], item[1]),
731	    ):
732	        before = before_rules.get(key)
733	        after = after_rules.get(key)
734	        if before is not None and after is not None and before == after:
735	            continue
736	        if before is None:
737	            kind = "added"
738	        elif after is None:
739	            kind = "removed"
740	        else:
741	            kind = "updated"
742	        expected_entries.append(
743	            {
744	                "source": key[0],
745	                "id": key[1],
746	                "kind": kind,
747	                "before": before,
748	                "after": after,
749	            }
750	        )
751	    if delta["rules"] != expected_entries:
752	        raise ValueError(
753	            f"{field}.delta.rules do not equal the diff of the adjacent "
754	            "snapshots"
755	        )
756	    before_identities = {_conflict_identity(c) for c in previous["conflicts"]}
757	    after_identities = {_conflict_identity(c) for c in point["conflicts"]}
758	    expected_added = [
759	        c for c in point["conflicts"] if _conflict_identity(c) not in before_identities
760	    ]
761	    expected_removed = [
762	        c for c in previous["conflicts"] if _conflict_identity(c) not in after_identities
763	    ]
764	    if (
765	        delta["conflicts"]["added"] != expected_added
766	        or delta["conflicts"]["removed"] != expected_removed
767	    ):
768	        raise ValueError(
769	            f"{field}.delta.conflicts do not equal the conflict identity "
770	            "diff of the adjacent snapshots"
771	        )
772	    if (
773	        not delta["rules"]
774	        and not delta["conflicts"]["added"]
775	        and not delta["conflicts"]["removed"]
776	    ):
777	        raise ValueError(f"{field}.delta must not be empty")
778

780	def _normalize_verified_schedule_report(
781	    report: Any, field: str
782	) -> dict[str, Any]:
783	    """Structurally and semantically validate a schedule attestation report.
784	
785	    Returns a fresh normalized copy with keys ``start``, ``end``, ``root``,
786	    ``points``. Every key-set, type, value-domain, time, snapshot, delta, and
787	    hash-chain-field-format rule of
788	    :func:`verify_policy_schedule_attestation` is enforced; the chain itself
789	    is recomputed separately by :func:`_recompute_schedule_root`. Any
790	    violation raises ``ValueError``.
791	    """
792	    if not isinstance(report, dict) or set(report) != set(
793	        _SCHEDULE_ATTEST_REPORT_KEYS
794	    ):
795	        raise ValueError(
796	            f"{field} must be a dict with exactly the keys "
797	            "start, end, root, points"
798	        )
799	    start = _check_time(report["start"], f"{field}.start")
800	    end = _check_time(report["end"], f"{field}.end")
801	    if start > end:
802	        raise ValueError(f"{field}.start must not be after {field}.end")
803	    root = _check_schedule_hex64(report["root"], f"{field}.root")
804	    points = report["points"]
805	    if not isinstance(points, list) or not points:
806	        raise ValueError(f"{field}.points must be a non-empty list")
807	    normalized_points: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
808	    previous_at: str | None = None
809	    for index, point in enumerate(points):
810	        normalized, at = _normalize_schedule_point(
811	            point, index, start, end, previous_at
812	        )
813	        _check_schedule_point_semantics(
814	            normalized, index, normalized_points[-1] if normalized_points else None
815	        )
816	        normalized_points.append(normalized)
817	        previous_at = at
818	    return {"start": start, "end": end, "root": root, "points": normalized_points}

821	def _recompute_schedule_root(points: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[bool, str]:
822	    """Recompute a schedule hash chain.
823	
824	    Returns ``(ok, root)`` where ``ok`` is ``False`` at the first broken
825	    ``previous``/``digest`` link and ``root`` is the running digest.
826	    """
827	    previous = _SCHEDULE_GENESIS
828	    for point in points:
829	        if point["previous"] != previous:
830	            return False, previous
831	        content = {key: point[key] for key in _SCHEDULE_POINT_CONTENT_KEYS}
832	        canonical = json.dumps(content, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
833	        digest = hashlib.sha256(
834	            previous.encode("ascii") + canonical.encode("utf-8")
835	        ).hexdigest()
836	        if point["digest"] != digest:
837	            return False, digest
838	        previous = digest
839	    return True, previous

842	def verify_policy_schedule_attestation(report: Any, expected: Any) -> bool:
843	    """Verify a :func:`policy_schedule_attestation` report by recomputation.
844	
845	    ``report`` must be a dict with exactly the keys ``start, end, root,
846	    points``; ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds with ``start <= end``,
847	    ``root`` 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, and ``points`` a non-empty
848	    list conforming level by level to the :func:`policy_schedule_attestation`
849	    contract (exact key sets, types, and value domains, including the
850	    :func:`compile_rules` rule/conflict shapes and the :func:`policy_delta`
851	    delta shape). The points' ``at`` values must be strictly increasing, lie
852	    in the closed interval ``[start, end]``, and the first point must have
853	    ``at == start`` and ``delta == null``; later points must carry a full
854	    delta. Each point's ``previous``/``digest`` must be 64 lowercase
855	    hexadecimal characters. ``expected`` must have exactly the keys
856	    ``start, end, root`` and is validated the same way. Any violation raises
857	    ``ValueError`` without mutating the inputs.
858	
859	    Each point is also checked against the schedule semantics: its ``rules``
860	    must be effective at its ``at`` (``from <= at < to`` or ``to`` null),
861	    unique per ``(source, id)``, and ranked exactly as :func:`compile_rules`
862	    ranks them (``law`` before ``org``, then ``priority`` descending,
863	    ``from`` descending, ``id`` in Unicode code point order, ``ver``
864	    descending); its ``conflicts`` must equal the conflicts derived from
865	    those rules (ranked indices ``i < j``, differing results, compatible
866	    ``when`` conditions, earlier rule wins) with none missing, forged,
867	    duplicated, or misordered. A later point's ``delta`` must span from the
868	    previous point's ``at`` to its own ``at`` and exactly match the
869	    :func:`policy_delta` of the two adjacent snapshots — ``rules`` ordered by
870	    ``source`` (``law`` before ``org``) then ``id`` in Unicode code point
871	    order, ``conflicts.added`` in the current point's conflict order and
872	    ``conflicts.removed`` in the previous point's — and must not be empty.
873	    Any semantic violation raises ``ValueError``.
874	
875	    Every dict is rebuilt in the contract key order (rule ``when`` keys in
876	    Unicode code point order) and the hash chain is recomputed exactly as
877	    :func:`policy_schedule_attestation` defines it: the first ``previous`` is
878	    64 ASCII ``0`` characters, every later ``previous`` is the preceding
879	    point's ``digest``, and each ``digest`` is the lowercase hexadecimal
880	    SHA-256 of ``previous``'s ASCII bytes immediately followed by the point's
881	    compact-JSON ``C`` over ``at, rules, conflicts, delta`` in that order.
882	
883	    Returns ``False`` when ``report`` and ``expected`` differ in ``start``,
884	    ``end``, or ``root``, or when any chain link, digest, or the final root
885	    does not match; otherwise ``True``. The function is pure: it touches no
886	    files and does not mutate its inputs.
887	    """
888	    normalized = _normalize_verified_schedule_report(report, "report")
889	    if not isinstance(expected, dict) or set(expected) != set(
890	        _SCHEDULE_ATTEST_EXPECTED_KEYS
891	    ):
892	        raise ValueError(
893	            "expected must be a dict with exactly the keys start, end, root"
894	        )
895	    expected_start = _check_time(expected["start"], "expected.start")
896	    expected_end = _check_time(expected["end"], "expected.end")
897	    if expected_start > expected_end:
898	        raise ValueError("expected.start must not be after expected.end")
899	    _check_schedule_hex64(expected["root"], "expected.root")
900	    if (
901	        normalized["start"] != expected_start
902	        or normalized["end"] != expected_end
903	        or normalized["root"] != expected["root"]
904	    ):
905	        return False
906	    ok, root = _recompute_schedule_root(normalized["points"])
907	    return ok and normalized["root"] == root
908

910	def explain(
911	    at: str, facts: dict[str, bool], rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
912	) -> dict[str, Any]:
913	    """Explain the decision :func:`evaluate` reaches for the same inputs.
914	
915	    Applies exactly :func:`evaluate`'s validation (raising ``ValueError`` on
916	    anything invalid), effective-window selection, latest-version retention,
917	    ranking, and matching, without mutating the inputs. The result is a deep
918	    copy with keys ``at``, ``decision``, ``trace``, ``basis``, ``conflicts``;
919	    ``decision`` and ``trace`` are exactly :func:`evaluate`'s outputs.
920	
921	    When nothing matches, ``basis`` is ``None`` and ``conflicts`` is empty.
922	    Otherwise ``basis`` is a snapshot of the top-ranked matching rule and
923	    ``conflicts`` keeps, in original order, the :func:`compile_rules`
924	    conflicts whose winner or loser equals
925	    ``[basis.source, basis.id, basis.ver]``.
926	    """
927	    _check_fact_map(facts, "facts")
928	    ranked = _effective_rules(at, rules)
929	    matched = [rule for rule in ranked if _matches(rule, facts)]
930	    if not matched:
931	        return {"at": at, "decision": None, "trace": [], "basis": None, "conflicts": []}
932	    basis = _snapshot_rule(matched[0])
933	    basis_key = [basis["source"], basis["id"], basis["ver"]]
934	    conflicts = [
935	        conflict
936	        for conflict in _find_conflicts(ranked)
937	        if conflict["winner"] == basis_key or conflict["loser"] == basis_key
938	    ]
939	    trace = [f"{rule['id']}@{rule['ver']}" for rule in matched]
940	    return {
941	        "at": at,

958

960	    :func:`explain`; any invalid time, fact type, rule structure, interval,
961	    or duplicate rule version raises ``ValueError`` without mutating the
962	    inputs. Only the passed values are used; no history or file is accessed.
963	
964	    Returns a deep copy with top-level keys ``at``, ``facts``,
965	    ``explanation``, ``policy``, ``digest``. ``facts`` is a deep copy of the
966	    input facts with keys sorted in Unicode code point order (an empty dict
967	    is valid); ``explanation`` is the full deep-copied :func:`explain`
968	    result at ``at`` keeping its canonical key order at every level;
969	    ``policy`` is the full deep-copied :func:`compile_rules` result at
970	    ``at``, conflicts included.

972	    Let ``C`` be the UTF-8 bytes of compact JSON (``ensure_ascii=False``,
973	    ``separators=(',', ':')``) over a payload containing exactly ``at``,
974	    ``facts``, ``explanation``, ``policy`` in that key order. ``digest`` is
975	    the lowercase 64-char hex SHA-256 of ``C``. Equal-valued inputs yield
976	    byte-identical attestations regardless of input dict key order; empty
977	    facts, empty rules, and no-match decisions all attest normally.

987	    canonical = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))

1111

1113	    nor files, and never mutates an input object at any level.
1114

1116	    ``explanation``, ``policy``, ``digest`` and conform level by level to the
1117	    :func:`decision_attestation` contract. ``at`` must be a valid UTC second;
1118	    ``facts`` must map non-empty string keys to bool values (an empty dict is
1119	    valid); ``digest`` must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. ``policy``
1120	    must have exactly the keys ``at``, ``rules``, ``conflicts`` with its
1121	    ``at`` equal to the report ``at``; its rules must be effective at that
1122	    time (``from <= at < to`` or ``to`` null), unique per ``(source, id)``,
1123	    and ranked exactly as :func:`compile_rules` ranks them, and its
1124	    ``conflicts`` must equal the conflicts fully rebuilt from those rules
1125	    (ranked indices ``i < j``, differing results, compatible ``when``
1126	    conditions, earlier rule wins) — missing, forged, duplicated, or
1127	    misordered entries are all illegal. ``explanation`` must have exactly the
1128	    keys ``at``, ``decision``, ``trace``, ``basis``, ``conflicts`` with its
1129	    ``at`` equal to the report ``at``; it is re-evaluated against the policy
1130	    rules with the report facts, so with no match ``decision``/``basis`` are
1131	    null and ``trace``/``conflicts`` empty, while with a match ``decision`` is
1132	    the top-ranked matching rule's result, ``trace`` lists every matching
1133	    rule, ``basis`` is that rule's snapshot, and ``conflicts`` keeps the
1134	    policy conflicts involving that basis in their original order.
1135	    ``expected`` must have exactly the keys ``at`` and ``digest``, validated

1139	    violation raises ``ValueError``. Both inputs complete structural and
1140	    semantic validation before any comparison, so a bad report is never

1143	    is recomputed as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the compact UTF-8

1166	        )

1277	def _rebuild_timeline_from_schedule(
1278	    start: str,
1279	    end: str,
1280	    facts: dict[str, bool],
1281	    policy: dict[str, Any],
1282	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1283	    """Rebuild the full decision timeline implied by an attested schedule.
1284	
1285	    The candidate timestamps are ``start`` plus every rule ``from``/non-empty
1286	    ``to`` boundary visible in the schedule's attested snapshots that falls in
1287	    ``(start, end]``; :func:`explain` is re-evaluated at each candidate with
1288	    the given facts, the first point is always kept, and later points are kept
1289	    exactly when a decision, trace, basis, or conflicts field changes — the
1290	    :func:`decision_timeline` rule.
1291	    """

1293	    seen: set[tuple[str, str, int]] = set()
1294	    for point in policy["points"]:
1295	        for rule in point["rules"]:
1296	            key = (rule["source"], rule["id"], rule["ver"])
1297	            if key not in seen:
1298	                seen.add(key)
1299	                rules.append(rule)
1300	    candidates = {start}
1301	    for rule in rules:
1302	        for boundary in (rule["from"], rule["to"]):
1303	            if boundary is not None and start < boundary <= end:
1304	                candidates.add(boundary)
1305	    first = explain(start, facts, rules)
1306	    points = [
1307	        {
1308	            "at": first["at"],
1309	            "decision": first["decision"],
1310	            "trace": first["trace"],
1311	            "basis": first["basis"],
1312	            "conflicts": first["conflicts"],
1313	            "changes": [],
1314	        }
1315	    ]
1316	    previous = first
1317	    for at in sorted(candidates - {start}):
1318	        report = explain(at, facts, rules)
1319	        changes = [
1320	            field for field in _COMPARE_FIELDS if previous[field] != report[field]
1321	        ]
1322	        if not changes:
1323	            continue
1324	        points.append(
1325	            {
1326	                "at": report["at"],
1327	                "decision": report["decision"],
1328	                "trace": report["trace"],
1329	                "basis": report["basis"],
1330	                "conflicts": report["conflicts"],
1331	                "changes": changes,
1332	            }
1333	        )
1334	        previous = report
